newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds face block at 114-27 but look up.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds face block at 114-27 but look up.

text.p: September T-bond futures will meet tough resistance at 114-27 on Thursday but once that is overcome there is scope to push higher, technical analysts said.

"The market is in overbought territory at 89.7 percent on the nine-day slow stochastics and will meet temporary tough resistance at 114-27," said Sam Malone-Jansens, analyst on the futures desk at Lloyds Bank in London.
"The risk/reward will probably favour some slippage, but in the bigger picture the uptrend is still intact."
At 1037 GMT September T-bond futures were hovering just below that level at 114-23, up 1/32 in automated trade.
Malone-Jansens said an 11-week trendline drawn through May 2's high at 109-29 and July 11's high at 114-15 came in at 114-27 which coincided with a tweezer top at 114-27 on hourly charts.
Below 114-27, there was light support at 114-22 with a firmer prop at 114-15, he said. Beyond there he saw further supports at 114-11 and 114-08.
To the upside, Malone-Jansens said once 114-27 was overcome, there was a resistance pivot point at 115-02 with a second resistance pivot point above there at 115-13.

"In the large picture the market retains the bullish edge and we had a positive signal on candlestick charts on Wednesday when we had a shaven white bottom, where the open was also the day's low, Malone-Jansens said.

Gerry Celaya, senior technical anlayst at American Express Bank in London said T-bond futures had broken higher on Wednesday as long-bond yield moved down below 6.50 percent and was now aiming for 6.30 percent.
"For the September contract this suggests that 116 and higher is open now," he said in a research note.
He set interim resistance at 114-27, 115-00 and 115-17.
December Eurodollars were at 94.075, up 0.010 on the day.
